summary.short: US federal statute requiring operators of child-directed online services, or those with actual knowledge of child users, to give notice and obtain verifiable parental consent before collecting personal information from children under 13. It directs FTC rulemaking and enforcement.
summary.long: This statute (15 U.S.C. 6501-6506) defines a child as an individual under 13 and an operator as a commercial website or online service operator that collects personal information online. Section 6502(a) makes it unlawful for such an operator, or one with actual knowledge of collecting from a child, to collect personal information from a child in violation of FTC regulations. Section 6502(b) requires the FTC, within one year of 21 October 1998, to issue rules requiring website notice of collection and use practices, verifiable parental consent, parental access and refusal rights, no conditioning of a child's participation on excess disclosure, and reasonable confidentiality and security procedures. The rules must set out exceptions for certain online contact information. Section 6502(c) treats a rule violation as an unfair or deceptive practice under the FTC Act. Section 6503 allows self-regulatory guidelines approved by the Commission to serve as deemed compliance, with action on requests within 180 days. Section 6504 lets state attorneys general sue in federal court for injunctions, enforcement, or damages on behalf of residents, after notice to the FTC. Section 6505 assigns enforcement to the FTC and to listed federal banking, transport and agricultural agencies. Section 6502(d) bars inconsistent state liability. Section 6506 requires an FTC review and a report to Congress within five years after the initial regulations take effect. Under the statutory notes, subsection (a) takes effect on the later of 18 months after enactment or the Commission's ruling on the first safe harbor application, and no later than 30 months after enactment.}},

notes: Text is the 2023 U.S. Code compilation of 15 U.S.C. 6501-6506 (no amendments shown). Regulations under §6502(b) are not part of this text. Footnote 2 in §6505(c) is flagged in the source as 'So in original. Probably should be subsection "(b)"'. Effective dates for §6502(a), §6504 and §6505 follow the Pub. L. 105–277 §1308 note (later of 18 months or the Commission's ruling on the first safe harbor application, not later than 30 months). No penalty amounts are stated in this chapter; penalties come through the FTC Act. The text neither creates nor excludes a private right of action. §6502(a)(2) limits liability for good-faith parental disclosures.

obligations.summary: Operators of websites or online services directed to children, or with actual knowledge of collecting personal information from a child, may not collect such information in a manner that violates the Commission's regulations under subsection (b).
obligations.conditional_on: Violation of regulations prescribed under §6502(b); applies to operators directed to children or with actual knowledge of collecting from a child.

evidence.quote: It is unlawful for an operator of a website or online service directed to children

obligations.summary: The Commission (FTC) must promulgate, under 5 U.S.C. 553, regulations requiring operators to give website notice of information collected, use and disclosure practices, to obtain verifiable parental consent, to give parents access and refusal rights, to bar conditioning participation on excess data disclosure, to require reasonable security procedures, and to permit service termination where a parent refuses.
obligations.applies_from: Not later than 1 year after October 21, 1998

obligations.summary: Under the required regulations, operators must provide notice on the website of what information is collected from children, how it is used, and their disclosure practices.

obligations.conditional_on: Operators of websites directed to children that collect personal information from children, or with actual knowledge of such collection.

evidence.quote: to provide notice on the website of what information is collected from children by the operator

obligations.summary: Under the required regulations, operators must obtain verifiable parental consent for the collection, use, or disclosure of personal information from children, subject to the exceptions in §6502(b)(2).

obligations.conditional_on: Operators of websites directed to children that collect personal information from children, or with actual knowledge of such collection; exceptions in §6502(b)(2).

obligations.summary: Under the required regulations, on parental request and proper identification, operators must describe the specific personal information collected from the child, allow the parent to refuse further use or collection, and provide a reasonable means for the parent to obtain the information.

obligations.conditional_on: Upon request of a parent whose child has provided personal information to the operator.

obligations.summary: Under the required regulations, operators may not condition a child's participation in a game, prize or other activity on the child disclosing more personal information than is reasonably necessary.
